page: Microsoft Azure E16d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor operating on the x86_64 architecture at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs split across 8 physical cores with two threads per core, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 vector instruction capabilities. System memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local temporary SSD storage of 644 GB is bundled with the instance, while discrete GPU hardware is absent.

Benchmark results place the instance in the middle tier for multi-core compute and data-handling throughput. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 7924.0, a PassMark CPU score of 15901.98, and static web serving throughput of 12.33 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 82.69 GB/sec alongside 44.34 GB/sec write bandwidth. In-memory data structures perform steadily, achieving 13.96 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. In contrast, single-core execution is lower, recording a stress-ng single-core score of 1411.58, and LLM text generation benchmarks remain limited due to CPU execution constraints.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16d_v4 offers strong memory density and fast local ephemeral storage without incurring the overhead of specialized accelerator hardware. It is suited for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational and non-relational database engines, data pipeline ETL tasks, and memory-intensive enterprise backends requiring high RAM capacity coupled with local scratch space.

Built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz across 8 physical cores with hyperthreading, the instance integrates 35 MB of L3 cache alongside 644 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Compute and memory benchmarks position the instance primarily in the middle tier, achieving 13.96 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, 12.33 GB/sec static web throughput, and 82.69 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. With no onboard GPU acceleration and lower single-core execution speed in stress-ng tests, this configuration prioritizes concurrent thread handling and memory capacity over raw single-threaded compute. The E16d_v4 fits production workloads such as in-memory data caching, relational databases, data processing, and enterprise backends requiring high RAM density and temporary local storage.
